name: context-consistency
content:
---
name: context-consistency
description: >
  Trace shared meanings and owners across Piik code, UI, copy and lifecycle.
  Use for cross-surface consistency work, recurring sibling-path defects or
  repository standardization audits; not every isolated edit.
---

# Context Consistency

Apply the project's [contextual contract](../../../docs/standards/engineering.md#contextual-consistency).
[AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) owns authority and
[CONTRIBUTING.md](../../../CONTRIBUTING.md) owns delivery. This skill is a review
method, not a second product specification or permission to change behavior.

## Scope And Sources

Read the user's latest accepted decisions and the relevant entries in the
[owner map](../../../docs/standards/documentation.md#owners). Follow their product, design,
engineering or operational owners; do not load every reference for a scoped fix.
Treat desired rules, current implementation and verified behavior separately.
An undocumented preference or an old audit is not an accepted contract.

For a scoped change, follow the affected semantic family and its actual callers.
For a requested repository-wide audit, first inventory standards and reachable
surfaces across Browser/App/Server, shared interfaces, website/demos, tooling
and guides. Record examined and unexamined areas so a large finding count cannot
stand in for coverage. Review-only work must not alter product sources.

## Trace Before Comparing

Follow a concrete producer through state/normalization, effects, consumers and
cleanup. Establish the subject, asserted fact or requested outcome, authority,
scope/generation, lifetime and user intent. Use a small comparison table only
when there are multiple variants to compare.

Ask whether an apparent inconsistency is:

- one meaning implemented or documented differently;
- different meanings accidentally using one label, flag or representation;
- a missing, conflicting or bypassed shared rule;
- an intentional adaptation supported by capability, authority or user context.

Compare timing as well as steady appearance: initial state, update, replacement,
failure/recovery and retirement. For async work, check A replaced by B before
A's completion or cleanup. For presentation, check actual state against copy,
icon, comic, mascot, motion and announcement, including simultaneous surfaces.
Do not infer progress from decoration, availability from configured capability,
or media readiness from signaling alone.

## Correct The Owning Boundary

When fixes are authorized, choose the smallest coherent correction at the
existing owner and update its reachable consumers. Share implementation where
the semantics and lifetime match; use narrow adapters for real runtime or
presentation differences. A similar name or repeated syntax is not sufficient
reason to merge states or introduce a generic manager. Visual consistency
preserves meaning and interaction without forcing every scene into one template.

If the intended semantics are unresolved, put that decision in
[TODO](../../../docs/todo.md) and continue independent checks. Do not turn a
proposal into a mandatory rule merely by adding it to a table.

Verify the changed producer-to-consumer boundary with existing previews, tests
or bounded runtime checks. Check that the correction preserves justified
differences and removes obsolete writers, mappings or timers. Stop broadening
verification after relevant checks pass unless new evidence warrants it.

## Deliver Useful Findings

Group occurrences by their root ownership or contract issue. Give each confirmed
finding its intended rule, reachable trigger, evidence, affected scope, smallest
correction and regression risk. Label unverified suspicions and design choices
separately. Do not claim a repository-wide pass from static searches or one view.

Use the existing owner map as the index of standards. Consolidating files must
preserve ownership, inbound links, tool-discovered paths and contributor entry
points; test those references after moves. Keep architectural rationale, user
guides and temporary audit evidence distinct from normative rules.

Absorb accepted lessons into their existing owner, keep remaining work in TODO,
and leave completed history in Git/PRs. Raw inventories, screenshots and audit
reports remain ignored working artifacts. Do not add a parallel permanent audit
ledger, scoring system, new dependency or extra approval flow.

name: ponytail
content:
---
name: ponytail
description: >
  Choose the smallest coherent implementation for Piik coding, code review,
  refactoring and implementation design, including dependency choices.
  Also use when Ponytail or YAGNI is requested; not for ordinary prose or status.
license: MIT
---

# Ponytail · Piik

Reduce what Piik must own while delivering the complete requested experience.
This is an implementation method under [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md), not
permission to reduce scope or defer design. The repo adaptation and license are
documented in [UPSTREAM.md](./UPSTREAM.md).

## Understand The Responsibility

Read the affected owner and actual flow before choosing a solution. Establish
the user outcome, state/resource lifetime and consumers that must keep working.
For a bug, trace where the incorrect fact or action first arises and check
sibling callers of that owner. Correct that boundary instead of adding a guard
to each symptom. A shared guard is useful only if it restores the real contract.

For UI, inspect the existing interaction and visual primitives before adding a
control, panel, status or animation. A reused component must still have the
right meaning, placement and lifecycle; reuse alone does not establish design
quality. Different responsibilities need not look or behave identically.

## Choose The Smallest Coherent Design

Use this order to find a sufficient solution, not as a mandatory research tour:

1. Remove speculative additions that the requested outcome does not need.
2. Reuse the existing owner, component or helper when its semantics and lifetime fit.
3. Prefer standard-library, native-platform or already-installed capabilities.
4. Use a mature dependency when it reduces total ownership more than custom code.
5. Implement the remaining behavior in a cohesive module with a narrow interface.

Compare user effort, state, dependencies and maintenance, not just lines or file
count. A larger correction is justified when it removes competing writers or
finishes the affected flow. Keep readable code and clear boundaries rather than
compressing logic into a one-liner or one oversized file.

Apply the shared [implementation rules](../../../docs/standards/engineering.md#implementation-rules)
for helper boundaries, typed validation, comments and generated sources rather
than maintaining separate coding rules in this skill. Preserve useful provenance
and required license notices when removing replaced paths.

## Verify And Finish

Verify the requested behavior at the affected boundary using the project's
existing checks. New mechanisms need evidence for their actual success,
failure and lifecycle behavior; a test for each branch or helper is not the
goal. Use [Stop That Shit](../stop-that-shit/SKILL.md) to keep verification
proportionate; required checks and delivery remain in
[CONTRIBUTING.md](../../../CONTRIBUTING.md).

Check the result against the intended experience and remove unnecessary
additions. Report the outcome, meaningful evidence and material limits at the
detail the user needs. Do not ship an easier subset as completion or impose a
fixed response length.

## Optional Intensity

Default **full** applies the method above. If requested, **lite** focuses on the
scoped implementation and obvious reuse; **ultra** more aggressively removes
unnecessary ownership within that scope. These levels change simplification
effort, never the requested result, design quality, authority or verification.

name: stop-that-shit
content:
---
name: stop-that-shit
description: >
  Keep Piik implementation, debugging and review proportionate and complete.
  Use to control speculative defenses, research or verification loops, and
  when Stop That Shit or removal of overengineering is requested.
license: MIT
---

# Stop That Shit · Piik

## 项目取舍

Piik 是供朋友分享的小项目。优先简单、好用、漂亮和实际效果，积极采用有收益的成熟方案与新技术。
不要按假想的百万级规模设计，不要追求覆盖一切极端情况、无限兼容或零风险。
复杂度、验证时间和维护负担都是真实成本。用户已经授权的合理工作，应当推进到可用结果。

这是工作尺度与收口方法；[Ponytail](../ponytail/SKILL.md) 负责实现取舍。
[AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) 规定权限与设计质量，
[CONTRIBUTING.md](../../../CONTRIBUTING.md) 规定交付流程。
新方法、新机制必须完整验证实际行为。减负不降低体验、审美或验证质量。

## 直接执行

- **让研究产生实现。** 参考相关的一手实现，选出简单、可逆的方案就做对照。
  一旦信息足够做决定，停止搜集同类材料。上游也有问题不等于只能接受；检查现有配置、
  接口和小范围补丁。研究或审查任务仍按其授权范围交付，不自动变成实现。
- **新机制要验完整。** 沿实际调用链验证预期效果及受影响的主路径，覆盖相关的失败、恢复
  和生命周期行为；不能用一个 happy path 或孤立单测宣称完成。复用现有检查和复现，缺口
  补有效回归。小文案、布局和可逆低影响改动不默认新增单元测试；不为每个分支、私有函数
  或实现细节各造一套测试。同一机制的不同检查应回答不同的实际问题。
- **已回答的问题不要反复验。** 相关代码、依赖、环境或证据没有变化，就复用有效结果。
  失败后检查具体原因；修正后重跑受影响部分。全套检查按交付阶段执行，不在每次小改后重跑。
  不为“再放心一点”追加矩阵、审计代理、证明文件或验证流程；明确要求的专项验收照常完成。
- **减负要真正删掉。** 在当前范围内移除已替代实现、重复防御、无消费者的产物和重复测试。
  不留注释代码、停用分支、过渡接口或长篇历史说明。仅用于本次调查的探针留在 ignored
  工作目录；值得长期保留的事实更新现有文档所有者，不再建一套审计账本。
- **交付有用结果。** 已授权的必要工作继续做，不停在计划、风险清单或“可以继续”。
  请求的体验与职责完整、相关检查通过且没有已知阻断就收口；不能以“能跑”代替验收。
  真正受阻时说明具体缺口和已尝试的方法。
  不把未知说成已解决，也不把所有未知都变成发布门槛。汇报结果和影响决定的限制即可，
  不用测试数量、长免责声明、反复道歉或未来待办替代成果。

参考来源与取舍保留在[上下文治理研究](../../../docs/research/agent-context-governance.md#instructions-and-skills)，
不作为每次任务必读材料。
